issues.description: The Meal constructor signature in the template does not match the problem specification and the solution. The UML and the solution expect Meal(String name, String[] ingredients), but the template declares Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). This mismatch will cause compilation errors with the provided Main examples and confuses students about the intended constructor parameter order.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Meal constructor in the template to match the specification and solution: public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) { ... }. Ensure any usages (e.g., in Main) follow the same parameter order.

issues.description: Constructor parameter order for the Meal class is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement's class diagram and the solution use Meal(String name, String[] ingredients), but the template declares the constructor as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). This mismatch breaks the direct mapping from the problem examples (and the solution) to the starter code and will cause compile errors/confusion when students try to use the example calls shown in the problem/Main.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template Meal constructor with the problem statement and solution by changing its signature to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and update any code/comments in the template that construct Meal accordingly (e.g., Main's example uses Meal("cowBoyStew", new String[]{...})).
